chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever drinks a draught of wine, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking wine on the acceptance of prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the penalty of forty days of rejected prayers for consuming a single draught of wine, highlighting the severity of *khamr* in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the spiritual impurity (*najis*) and physical intoxication that disrupts the connection between the worshipper and Allah, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic prohibition of intoxicants.
